evidence: The Interior Minister formally chairs the Higher Council. Traffic Law art. 17 bis mandates a national strategy and executive plan, coordination of relevant agencies and legislative proposals.
qualification: Statutory chair/coordination role; not sole execution authority

evidence: The July 2025 approved plan reportedly contains funding sources for 50 projects and 28 programmes, and the council discussed agencies’ 2026 budget needs. No Finance Ministry seat or verified approved joint results-based council budget.
qualification: Budget interfaces, not a formal Finance Ministry seat or full funding proof

evidence: Director of Public Security and an appointed deputy are statutory council members; police are an operational enforcement agency and reported smart camera, safety-belt and violation monitoring.
qualification: Formal policing seats; individual enforcement belongs to PSD

evidence: Article 17 bis authorizes the council to propose amendments to traffic-safety legislation. No separate Ministry of Justice representative or council adjudication function verified; 2023 law reforms predated the 2024 regulation.
qualification: Legal-policy proposal function, not justice-system membership

evidence: The council reviewed a reported rise in first-aid training and police-led post-crash safety activity; the Public Security Directorate also includes civil-defence capacities, but the council’s own extrication/fire-service action owner is N/A.
qualification: Narrow first-aid/emergency delivery link, not a fire-service seat or complete rescue mandate

evidence: Private-sector seats exist without a verified vehicle-manufacturer designation. The separate Central Technical Office’s vehicle design/manufacturing duties must not be counted as a Higher Council industry seat.

Ministry of Public Works and Housing Secretary-General is a statutory council member, providing an official public-works/civil-engineering portfolio link and delivery responsibilities for hazard treatment.
qualification: Formal public-works portfolio; no separate engineering trade association

evidence: Public Works and Housing is a statutory council member; the council reviewed and monitored remediation of black spots and governorate road signs and safety barriers.
qualification: Formal road-works ministry; road projects delivered by responsible agencies

evidence: Ministry of Transport Secretary-General and Land Transport Regulatory Commission Director-General formally participate; Transport Ministry representatives report helping prepare the 2024–2028 national road-safety strategy.
qualification: Formal transport regulation and service portfolios

evidence: Article 17 bis authorizes a road traffic information/statistics database; PSD presented smart camera and traffic management technology to the council. A completed interoperable national crash/exposure data platform is not verified.
qualification: Data/digital function, no dedicated digital ministry seat

evidence: No Environment Ministry seat or distinct environment-sector road-safety implementation mandate was identified in the council statute or the reviewed approval notice.
qualification: Other transport sustainability projects are not council duties

evidence: The Ministry of Local Administration Secretary-General and Greater Amman City Manager are statutory council members; Jordan also has a local-administration Road Safety Committee coordinating municipal work with the Higher Council.
qualification: Formal local-government members; municipal committee is a separate body

evidence: Council review of national first-aid training output and police/first-response monitoring evidences a limited care-related programme link; no Ministry of Health seat or nationwide trauma/rehabilitation responsibility is established.
qualification: Care-related programme coordination, not health ministry board representation

evidence: Two private-sector representatives are statutory council members and the council coordinates official and civic bodies; municipal committees run community awareness activities. Private-sector representation is not proof of a community-association seat.
qualification: Statutory private sector and external awareness links, not named local community organization representation

evidence: Council-reviewed awareness outputs, municipal school/community activities and first-aid training document education and training functions. No Ministry of Education council seat or nationwide curriculum obligation verified.
qualification: Education campaigns and local school outreach, not formal education-ministry seat

evidence: No council-linked social-protection, trauma rehabilitation or crash-victim benefit programme was established from the reviewed mandate and progress reports.
qualification: Insurance requirements in general traffic law do not prove victim support through this council

evidence: National crisis/evacuation responsibilities exist elsewhere, but a specific civil-defence disaster or mass-casualty evacuation mandate attributable to this council was not verified.
qualification: Public-security membership does not automatically prove disaster preparedness action
